newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to unveil $1 billion in Detroit investments.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to unveil $1 billion in Detroit investments.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. Chairman Robert Eaton is expected to unveil Wednesday a total of $1 billion in new investments at the automaker's assembly and component plants around the Detroit area, the company and analysts said.

Chrysler officials declined to elaborate on the scope of the investments, which were described Tuesday as "significant." Eaton will detail the plans at a press briefing at the company's Mack Avenue Engine Plant at 10 a.m. (EDT). Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer also will be present.

Mike Robinet, managing director of CSM Forecasting, a Farmington Hills, Mich., industry consultant, said the centerpiece of the $1 billion in investments will be a production capacity boost at the Jefferson North Assembly Plant, which produces the Jeep Grand Cherokee sport utility vehicle.

The plant's body and paint shops will be expanded to allow production of about 75 vehicles an hour from 51, raising the plant's straight-time production capacity to more than 300,000 vehicles per year from 260,000 a year currently, said Robinet.
"It'll turn Jefferson North into one of the largest assembly plants in North America," he said.
With overtime and the addition of a third shift, the plant could build as many as 360,000 Grand Cherokees a year.

The U.S. No. 3 automaker has been reaping huge rewards from the booming popularity of highly profitable light truck products such as pickup trucks, minivans and sport utility vehicles. About two-thirds of Chrysler's sales currently come from the segment.

Chrysler also is expected to expand the Mack Avenue engine plant, which is slated to start production of a new generation of truck engines next year. In 1995, Chrysler said it would spend $750 million to rennovate the existing Mack Avenue plant to build new six- and eight-cylinder engines.

In addition to Mack Avenue and Jefferson North, the automaker's other Detroit facilities include the Conner Avenue assembly operation; the Mound Road and Detroit Axle powertrain plants; the Mount Elliot tool and die facility; and the McGraw Glass operation.
Separately, in move to protect its dominance of the U.S. minivan market, Chrysler said Tuesday it is offering a new $595 cash incentive on minivans equipped with a left-side sliding door.

The consumer incentive program runs from Tuesday, April 8, through July 7. It replaces an "owner loyalty" incentive program that offered rebates of $500 to $750 only to owners of Chrysler's 1984-96 model minivans, which expired on Monday.

The new program, available to anyone, offers $595 in cash to buyers of 1996 and 1997 Dodge Caravan and Grand Caravan, Plymouth Voyager and Grand Voyager, and Chrysler Town & Country minivans equipped with driver-side sliding doors.

The rebate, the first national incentive on Chrysler's minivans since they were redesigned for the 1996 model year, completely offsets the price of the left-side door on vehicles that offer it as an option. The incentive also is available on vehicles that offer the door as standard equipment.

"We're determined to maintain our position as the automotive industry's minivan leader by continuing to offer the best vehicles and the best values, said James Holden, Chrylser's executive vice president of sales and marketing. "This program helps us do that."
